title: John Chrysostom on 2 Thessalonians 1:1
body: “The greater part of men do and devise all things with a view to ingratiate themselves with rulers, and with those who are greater than themselves; and they account it a great thing, and think themselves happy, if they can obtain that object. But if to obtain favor with men is so great an advantage, how great must it be to find favor with God?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 2
bodyEs: “La mayor parte de los hombres hacen y traman todas las cosas con miras a congraciarse con los gobernantes, y con los que son mayores que ellos; y lo tienen por cosa grande, y se creen felices, si pueden obtener ese objeto. Pero si hallar favor con los hombres es una ventaja tan grande, ¿cuán grande ha de ser hallar favor con Dios?”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Thessalonians 1:9
body: “There are many men, who form good hopes not by abstaining from their sins, but by thinking that hell is not so terrible as it is said to be, but milder than what is threatened, and temporary, not eternal; and about this they philosophize much. But I could show from many reasons, and conclude from the very expressions concerning hell, that it is not only not milder, but much more terrible than is threatened.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 3
bodyEs: “Hay muchos hombres que se forman buenas esperanzas no absteniéndose de sus pecados, sino pensando que el infierno no es tan terrible como se dice, sino más suave de lo que se amenaza, y temporal, no eterno; y acerca de esto filosofan mucho. Pero yo podría mostrar con muchas razones, y concluir por las mismas expresiones acerca del infierno, que no solo no es más suave, sino mucho más terrible de lo que se amenaza.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Thessalonians 2:6
body: “One may naturally enquire, what is that which withholdeth, and after that would know, why Paul expresses it so obscurely. What then is it that withholdeth, that is, hindereth him from being revealed?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 4
bodyEs: “Naturalmente puede uno preguntar qué es aquello que detiene, y después de eso querría saber por qué Pablo lo expresa tan oscuramente. ¿Qué es, pues, lo que detiene, esto es, lo que le impide ser revelado?”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Thessalonians 3:3
body: “Neither ought we, having committed everything to the prayers of the Saints, to be idle ourselves, and run into wickedness, and to lay hold of nothing; nor again when working good to despise that succor. For great indeed are the things which prayer for us can effect, but it is when we ourselves also work.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 5
bodyEs: “Tampoco debemos, habiendo encomendado todo a las oraciones de los santos, quedarnos ociosos nosotros, y correr a la maldad, y no asirnos de nada; ni tampoco, al obrar el bien, despreciar aquel auxilio. Porque grandes son, sí, las cosas que la oración por nosotros puede lograr, pero es cuando nosotros también trabajamos.”
